extracted.intended_audience: Federal departments and agencies of the Government of Canada responsible for developing, managing, and reviewing federal regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Directive-level requirements and standards for the full life cycle of Canadian federal regulations: development, management, consultation, analysis, publication, implementation and review. Focused on how departments and agencies must design regulatory proposals and supporting analyses to meet Treasury Board expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability / Scope of the Directive
rubrics_metrics.description: This directive applies to all regulations that are or will be registered as such under section 6 of the Statutory Instruments Act, made by or with the approval of the Governor in Council, the Treasury Board, or a minister of the Crown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation-making authorities for other regulations are strongly encouraged to follow and apply this directive to the greatest extent possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory purpose and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations must be justified by a clear rationale in terms of protecting the health, safety, security, social and economic well-being of Canadians, and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departments and agencies must demonstrate through the best available evidence and analysis that government intervention is needed to address identified public policy issues and risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principles — public interest and good government
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations protect and advance the public interest and support good government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations should be justified by a clear rationale focused on public well‑being (health, safety, security, socio-economic well‑being) and environmental protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principles — modern, open, and transparent process
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulatory process is modern, open, and transparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations and related activities must be accessible and understandable, created, maintained and reviewed in an open, transparent, and inclusive way that meaningfully engages the public and stakeholders, including Indigenous peoples, early on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principles — evidence-based decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory decision-making is evidence-based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and decisions must be based on evidence, robust analysis of costs and benefits, and assessment of risk, while being open to public scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principles — support fair and competitive economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations support a fair and competitive economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations should aim to support inclusive economic growth, entrepreneurship and innovation; consider regulatory cooperation and alignment to reduce burden while maintaining or improving health, safety and environmental standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory life-cycle approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations must be examined and analyzed through all stages of their life cycle: development, regulatory management, and review and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During all stages regulators must seek opportunities to engage stakeholders (including Indigenous peoples), pursue regulatory cooperation/alignment, and coordinate with other levels of government to minimize cumulative and unintended impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder identification and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments and agencies are responsible for identifying stakeholders impacted by regulations, including Indigenous peoples, and meaningfully consulting and engaging with them throughout the development, management, and review of regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Government of Canada policies/guidance for consultation; document comments received and make them available on request; use modern, digital, accessible and secure platforms; consider accessibility limitations for stakeholders, including Indigenous peoples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to consult Indigenous peoples (Crown’s legal duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proposed regulations may adversely impact potential or established Aboriginal or treaty rights under section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982, departments and agencies must satisfy the Crown’s duty to consult and, where appropriate, accommodate those rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage early and appropriately; follow consultation duties in law and policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory cooperation — assessment and pursuit
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments and agencies are to assess opportunities for cooperation with other jurisdictions, domestically and internationally, on regulations and associated activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine alignment with trading partners to reduce regulatory burden while maintaining or improving protections; consider international standard development organizations and formal cooperative arrangements; provide rationale where Canada-specific approaches are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory alignment — definition and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory alignment occurs when agreements or arrangements reduce or eliminate differences between independent regulatory systems and activities (inspections, certification, standards, approvals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alignment where appropriate to reduce differences and duplication while upholding standards of public health, safety and environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination across departments and jurisdictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments and agencies are responsible for working with each other to coordinate regulatory efforts within the Government of Canada when engaging with stakeholders, including Indigenous peoples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine ways to reduce duplication, promote efficiencies, share information, consider cumulative impacts, and reduce reporting and administrative burdens where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments must identify public policy issues to be addressed, outline risks to health, safety, security, economy, social and economic well‑being and environment, and demonstrate with best available evidence that government intervention is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where threats of serious or irreversible harm exist, lack of full scientific certainty must not be used to postpone cost‑effective measures to prevent harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument choice (regulatory vs non-regulatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments must assess the effectiveness and appropriateness of regulatory and non‑regulatory instruments to achieve policy objectives and consult stakeholders as part of this exercise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider domestic and international best practices; document instrument choice results in the RIAS where appropriate; examine costs and benefits of options; favor outcome/performance‑based regulations when appropriate to minimize burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design outcome/performance-based regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: When appropriate, regulations should be outcome or performance-based, specifying desired results rather than prescriptive compliance steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome-based regulations increase flexibility for regulated parties and focus on achieving specific and measurable outcomes while minimizing regulatory burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward Regulatory Plan (advance notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments should provide advance notice to stakeholders of upcoming regulatory changes over a 24‑month period and update Forward Regulatory Plans annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders may comment on Forward Regulatory Plans; initial consultation on instrument choice should occur before incorporation into the Plan; regulatory proposals should be included in the Plan before pre‑publication in Canada Gazette Part I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations prior to pre-publication
rubrics_metrics.description: During development departments should consult and engage appropriate stakeholders (including Indigenous peoples and trading partners); the size and scope of consultations is the department’s responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre‑publication in Canada Gazette Part I is not a substitute for early consultation; do not postpone pre‑publication due to unanimity of views; view engagement as an ongoing dialogue with multiple tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments and agencies must conduct a Regulatory Impact Analysis on all regulatory proposals to support stakeholder engagement and evidence‑based decision‑making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RIA is a systematic identification and critical assessment of potential positive and negative effects on the public, stakeholders and Cabinet; comply with relevant acts, Treasury Board policies, and engage TBS Regulatory Affairs Sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIA — scope of impacts to examine
rubrics_metrics.description: RIA must examine potential positive and negative effects on the health, safety, security, social and economic well‑being of Canadians, businesses, and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include qualitative and quantitative analysis proportional to expected impact; demonstrate that benefits to Canadians outweigh the costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triage — early assessment of impact level
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments must conduct an early assessment (triage) to determine expected impact level and appropriate analytical requirements for the RIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use triage to determine mix of analytical elements proportional to the proposal’s expected impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIA — impacts on Canadians (specific indicators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider impacts on well‑being (health, safety, security, ability to make informed choices), consumer impacts (cost of living, prices, quality and variety), income and employment opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess distribution of impacts across groups; include both positive and negative effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIA — impacts on businesses (specific indicators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider costs of complying with regulatory requirements including administrative burden, changes in profit and revenue, business opportunities/growth/innovation, business sustainability, and costs to implement/administer regulatory programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify administrative burdens explicitly and quantify where possible; include compliance and enforcement, outreach, data management and event response costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIA — impacts on government
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider costs and benefits for other levels of government (provincial, territorial, Indigenous, municipal) and impacts on government revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess cross‑jurisdictional implications and fiscal effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of benefits and costs / cost-benefit analysis (CBA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments must examine potential positive and negative impacts of a proposed regulation and feasible alternatives on Canadians, businesses, governments and the environment using structured CBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When quantification is not possible, provide a rigorous qualitative analysis; CBA helps decision‑makers determine the best course of action; regulators must demonstrate benefits outweigh costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of environmental impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments are to undertake an assessment of potential environmental effects for each regulatory proposal when appropriate and in accordance with the Cabinet Directive on the Environmental Assessment of Policy, Plan and Program Proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine likely effects (positive/negative), need for mitigation/enhancement, and importance of adverse effects taking mitigation into account; use this to inform the public that environmental factors were considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender-based analysis plus (GBA+)
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments must undertake an assessment of social and economic impacts on diverse groups of Canadians using GBA+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GBA+ examines impacts beyond sex and gender to include multiple intersecting identity factors (race, ethnicity, religion, age, disabilities, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimizing burden on business (One-for-One Rule & small business focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments must comply with the One‑for‑One Rule and estimate administrative burden impacts on Canadian businesses, aiming to minimize burden without compromising protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider specific impacts on small businesses to avoid disproportionate burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory cooperation analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine regulatory systems of relevant jurisdictions (domestic partners, trading partners) to identify alignment or cooperation opportunities, and review international standards for possible incorporation by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where differences are required, provide a rationale for a Canada‑specific approach; consider formal coordinated arrangements and established procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference — accessibility and language obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: When incorporating external standards or documents by reference, departments must ensure incorporated documents are accessible, easily understood, and respect constitutional language obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain in the RIAS why incorporation by reference is used; ensure bilingual incorporation or legitimate reason for unilingual; regularly review incorporated material to keep it up to date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of modern treaty implications (AMTI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments must undertake an Assessment of Modern Treaty Implications and respect law‑making authorities and rights of modern treaty partners and self‑governing Indigenous groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage implicated modern treaty partners on AMTI findings where implications are identified and ensure Government meets treaty/self‑government obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of international obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments must ensure Canada’s international commitments (human rights, health, safety, trade, environment) are met and consider international consultation/notification requirements in regulatory development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure international commitments are implemented when carrying out regulatory activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments must plan for implementation of regulatory proposals as part of their analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider implications for other jurisdictions, timing, infrastructure requirements (IM/IT), fund sources, compliance promotion and outreach, up‑to‑date guidance/technical documents, enforcement plans, training, and possible evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Impact Analysis Statement (RIAS) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments must develop a RIAS in accordance with Policy on Regulatory Development; a RIAS is a clear, non‑technical synthesis of expected impacts based on the RIA and is published with regulatory text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RIAS must synthesize analyses for public and stakeholder consideration and accompany pre‑publication and final publication as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication requirements and comment periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre‑publication (Canada Gazette Part I) submissions must include draft regulatory text and a RIAS; the standard comment period is 30 days unless otherwise prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A minimum 70‑day comment period may be required for new/amended technical regulations with significant effect on international trade (WTO TBT obligations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from pre-publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemptions from pre‑publication may be granted when there is no statutory requirement to pre‑publish, by Treasury Board or relevant authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not pre‑published, include a brief rationale for the exemption in the final RIAS as best practice; consult the Regulatory Affairs Sector when considering an exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final publication and statutory registration
rubrics_metrics.description: All approved regulations must be published in the Canada Gazette Part II after they are made and registered, except where exempted under the Statutory Instruments Regulations; a RIAS must be included with published regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Statutory Instruments Act requirements for registration and coming into force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional measures (exemptions for urgent circumstances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemptions from certain regulatory development requirements may be granted by Treasury Board, Cabinet or relevant authority in cases of serious and immediate risk to health/safety/security/environment/economy, internal reorganizations, or other exceptional circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Regulatory Affairs Sector when considering seeking an exemption for an exceptional measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing regulatory management responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments are responsible for ongoing management of regulations and associated programs to improve effectiveness in meeting objectives (compliance, inspections, licensing, outreach, data gathering, performance measurement, clear information to Canadians).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure no contradictions between guidance/technical documents and regulations; keep guidance consistent with existing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing predictability — service standards and guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments must develop, publish and review service standards for high‑volume regulatory transactions and publish guidelines to clarify regulatory requirements and improve information sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service standards promote timeliness and provide clear expectations for interactions and service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance and enforcement strategy design
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments must develop and implement compliance and enforcement strategies/programs to promote effectiveness of regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategies should consider risk‑based approaches; allocate resources to most significant risks; avoid duplication by coordinating across governments; proactively engage regulated communities and provide clear, up‑to‑date guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews of regulatory programs (performance evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments are responsible for evaluating performance of regulatory programs and must adhere to the Treasury Board Policy on Results and Policy on Internal Audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes of program reviews can inform regulatory stock reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular review of the regulatory stock
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments must regularly review existing regulatory stock (including technical guidance and associated policies) to ensure regulations remain appropriate and effective and achieve intended objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While reviewing, examine removing obsolete regulations, determining effectiveness, mitigating unintended impacts (barriers to trade/innovation), ensuring technical standards are accurate and up to date, demonstrating cost‑effectiveness, identifying burden‑reduction opportunities, minimizing impacts on small business, and amending to resolve enforcement issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of review plans in Forward Regulatory Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Review plans and planned amendments identified as part of review processes should be published annually in Forward Regulatory Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results of reviews should inform future regulatory development to continue the life cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to the Standing Joint Committee for the Scrutiny of Regulations (SJCSR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments must respond to issues raised by the SJCSR in a timely manner; communications should be responsive and constructive and actions implemented promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SJCSR scrutinizes regulations to ensure they respect enabling powers and drafting standards; every statutory instrument is referred to SJCSR for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory Instruments Act and avoidance of inappropriate exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations are statutory instruments under the Statutory Instruments Act; regulations should not be exempted from those requirements except in exceptional circumstances approved by Cabinet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeking exemptions to avoid the Cabinet Directive is not justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat (TBS) roles and quality assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: TBS provides advice/guidance, supports ministerial decision‑making and oversight, reviews regulatory proposals, challenges departments on quality of analyses, and assesses directive implementation effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TBS promotes policy coherence, is a source of good regulatory practices expertise, and leads stakeholder education and maintenance of supporting policies, guidance and tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privy Council Office (PCO) roles — examination, registration, consolidation
rubrics_metrics.description: PCO assesses memoranda to Cabinet and legislative proposals for instrument selection and regulatory implications; examines regulations with Department of Justice; registers regulations and can refuse registration if Statutory Instruments Act requirements were not followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCO registers regulations within seven days after making; requires justification for early coming into force; prepares quarterly consolidated index; can request revisions or consolidations after consultation with Deputy Minister of Justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Justice role — legal review and drafting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of Justice provides legal advice on legality of enabling and subordinate legislation, drafts instruments, and examines proposed regulations to ensure legal authority, Charter/Bill of Rights consistency, no unusual use of authority, and drafting standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides legal tools/advice on instruments, regulatory techniques, international obligations; Trade Law Bureau advises on trade law obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canada Gazette Directorate responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Services and Procurement Canada’s Canada Gazette Directorate is responsible for publishing the Canada Gazette (formal public notices, proposed regulations, regulations) and ensuring a rigorous publication process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canada Gazette provides consultative tool for Canadians to comment on proposed regulations; the Directorate ensures strict publication deadlines and handles background information requests from affected parties.
